notes:
THE ROW THAT BOUNDS delta_s FROM BELOW. Nothing else measured does.

A pale callout box is structurally identical to a highlight: a bright saturated fill with dark text on it. The fill rule cannot reject it -- it IS bright. Coverage cannot reject it -- it IS fully covered. Even a stroke-aware text mask cannot reject it, because it really is a fill with glyphs on top. Nothing in the detector distinguishes it except saturation.

It escapes today by 0.054. The fill measures S 0.196 against a cut of paper+0.25 = 0.250. The palest REAL highlight measured, Kindle's at row 11, starts at 0.27. So:

    delta_s must be ABOVE 0.196  (or this page imports its callout boxes)
    delta_s must be BELOW 0.27   (or Kindle highlights stop being found)

A window about 0.074 wide. 0.25 sits in it, with 0.054 below and only 0.02 above. Before this page there was no lower bound at all, and lowering delta_s to widen the Kindle margin would have looked free.

Note the paper estimate matters here: the median S of bright pixels is 0.106 because the boxes are large enough to drag it, which would have moved the cut to 0.356 and hidden the problem. The MODE of near-white pixels gives 0.000, which is the truth. F1 says median; on a page like this that is the wrong statistic.
